text:
sam: heads-up — hosted-prod p99 jumped to ~3.6s (was ~600ms) starting ~2026-03-17T12:02:00Z. p95 also up. Affected mostly shard-3 and shard-7. Queue depth on those nodes hit ~120. Seeing a lot of `enqueue_delay` in the route logs. Anyone already looking?

anya: looking at KV cache metrics -> eviction rate spiked and hit_rate dropped ~12% around the same time. Could be priming/thrashing. sample log lines: 
```
2026-03-17T12:02:11Z KV_EVICT shard=3 key=tenant123 evict_ms=12 count=84
2026-03-17T12:02:12Z KV_LOOKUP shard=3 key=tenantXYZ miss=true
```

jordan: I pulled a tracing window. We're seeing kernel_selector churn: requests for the same route are flipping between `aux_kernel_v2` and `aux_kernel_v1` mid-burst because the sampler splits batches due to a long-short-long sequence pattern. trace snippet: 
```
kernel_choice: aux_v1 -> batch_size 4 -> short seq
kernel_choice: aux_v2 -> batch_size 16 -> long seq
kernel_choice: aux_v1 -> batch_size 3 -> short seq
```

li: That kernel heuristic was adjusted in yesterday's rollout (rollout id=2026-03-17-kerheur). If the sampler produces interleaved seq lengths it can oscillate. Combined with KV cache churn (many prefetches), the runtime ends up doing extra kernel warmups + cache evictions => tail latency.

perf-bot: automated-profile summary (12:02-12:05): `kernel_switch_cpu=42%`, `io_wait=28%`, `gpu_busy=15%`, `other=15%`. Hot functions: `select_kernel()`, `kv_prefetch()`, `batch_sampler()`.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-234 created and page sent to oncall.

sam: can we reproduce in staging with the same replay? jordan?

jordan: pushed a replay of the request pattern to staging (replay-id r-5612). reproduces p99 spike when bursts contain long-short-long. Repro script: 
```
replay-tool --id r-5612 --rate 200 --pattern long,short,long --dest staging-hosts
```
Observed batching sampler cut into 3 batches causing two kernel switches per burst. Also saw KV prefetch queue growing.

anya: kvcache prefetch counters during replay: `prefetch_miss_rate` rose from 2% -> 18%. Eviction churn timeline matches p99 spike. Short requests lose cache locality.

li: short-term mitigation: pin kernel to `aux_v2` on affected shards and increase kvcache TTL to reduce eviction churn for those tenants. We can roll that as a config flag per-route. Will prepare hotfix flag: `--kernel-pin=aux_v2` and `--kvcache-ttl=60s`.

sam: status? canary first? :eyes:

jordan: rolling canary to 3 nodes in shard-3 now with flags. deploy command: 
```
deploy-tool canary --env hosted-prod --shards shard-3 --envvars "KERNEL_PIN=aux_v2,KVCACHE_TTL=60"
```

perf-bot: canary metrics (12:10-12:14): canary nodes p99 -> 720ms (from 3.6s), p95 -> 210ms. Non-canary still elevated.

anya: after canary hit, kvcache hit_rate on canary nodes improved ~9%. eviction rate dropped ~50% on those hosts.

li: good signal. I'll open a rollback/feature-flag so we can pin while we root-cause the heuristic change. Need permanent fix: make sampler aware of within-burst seq-length variance and avoid splitting batches that cause kernel switches.

sam: agreed. immediate plan: 1) expand kernel pin + ttl to affected shards, 2) monitor for 30m, 3) roll to rest of affected shards if stable. 4) post-incident follow-ups: improve sampler heuristics, gate kernel-heuristic rollout with watch thresholds, and add kvcache priming monitor. Owners: li (kernel heuristics), anya (kvcache/tuning), jordan (sampler & deploy).

jordan: FYI I added a temporary monitor: `runtime.kernel_switch_rate` alert > 5/min for a shard triggers page.

oncall-bot: INC-2026-234 status -> mitigated (canary shows improvement).

sam: follow-up tickets:
- PERF-814: batching sampler: avoid churn on long-short-long patterns (li)
- PERF-815: kvcache priming backpressure and prefetch smoothing (anya)
- OPS-662: rollout-gate for kernel-heuristic changes + canary metrics (jordan)

li: also plan to add a small experiment: fallback_quiet_window after kernel switch to avoid immediate flip-flop. will prototype.

anya: good. I'll schedule a retro and add the pre/post metric graphs to the incident. :rocket:

sam: thanks all. keep updates here for the 30m watch.
